title: SportsCapping Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Is It Worth It?
description: SportsCapping review, checked 20 Nov 2026: a 76 handicapper pick marketplace, picks from $25 to $50, $199 Monthly Club, replacement guarantee, records checked.
dek: A pick marketplace that says it has sold picks since 2003 and lists 76 handicappers. Single picks on the 20 Nov 2026 board cost $25 to $50, and a Monthly Club runs $199. Losing guaranteed packages earn a free replacement package, not cash, and every record on the site is graded by SportsCapping itself. Its own 2026 board shows the most profitable handicapper at a 3.2% return.

short_answer: SportsCapping is a real, working marketplace. On 20 Nov 2026 its board listed 566 picks from 63 handicappers, prices were posted for every package, and the FAQ names Boyd Information Group as the company that bills buyers. A BBB complaint in 2026 was answered and resolved. In that narrow sense it is legitimate.

Whether its handicappers make money for buyers is a different question. The site says every record is verified and its Google Play listing calls the records "independently tracked," but the grading is done by SportsCapping, the company that earns money on every sale. We found no outside monitor.

Its own numbers are the best reason for caution. The pick listings lead with 30 day windows such as 27-10 or 23-9, but the 2026 season board shows the top handicapper by profit at a 3.2% return, and the median of the 31 handicappers shown at 1.3%. Several featured handicappers had fewer than half of their weeks in profit.

Buyer feedback is small and mostly negative: App Store reviews from 2015 to 2025 complain about losing picks and slow email support, with two positive reviews, and one 2026 BBB complaint about a season pass that was charged but not switched on, later fixed. If you buy, buy short, log every pick yourself and judge a handicapper over hundreds of plays.

guarantee: The About page says: "If a guaranteed package doesn't profit, you automatically get the next day of picks free; guaranteed subscriptions extend for the same length." The FAQ adds: "No claim needed. Guarantees are tracked automatically" and the make good is applied to your account on its own. A guarantee badge shows on each package that has one.

That is a replacement, not a refund. It never covers the money lost on the bets themselves, which is usually far more than the pick price, and the replacement comes from the same handicapper, so it can lose too. On cash refunds the FAQ says only: "Because picks are graded results, refunds are reviewed individually."

Billing: the FAQ says "there is no auto-renewal and no recurring billing," and that charges appear as Boyd Information Group. The Monthly Club page data did show a renewal date of 20 Dec 2026, so check your order page after buying to confirm nothing renews.

The Terms of Use say the site is provided "as is" and "as available," that the terms are governed by Iowa law with disputes in Iowa courts, and that any claim "must be filed within one (1) year after the incident, or it is permanently barred."

claims_note: How we checked: every handicapper listing on the homepage carries a short window record, usually the last 30 days in one sport, plus a count of winning weeks or seasons. We set those side by side, and then against the 2026 season leaderboard, which covers 1 Jan to 20 Nov 2026 on flat $100 bets. The pattern is consistent: the headline window is always the best looking slice. Mike Lundin's 27-10 sits next to 6 winning weeks out of 18; Sean Murphy's 11-1-1 run sits next to 8 of 21.

The season board puts those windows in context. The most profitable handicapper of 2026, Brooke Bennett, was 1220-1092-56 for $8,571, which is 52.8% and a 3.2% return. Among the 31 handicappers shown, the best return was 9.0%, on only 164 picks, and the median was 1.3%. A buyer who pays $25 to $50 per pick needs a far bigger edge than that to come out ahead after the price.

The site states its own method: records cover each handicapper's premium picks, and figures labelled "Best Run" or "since" a date show a window starting on the date shown, "not a lifetime record." That is an honest label, and it also confirms the headline numbers are chosen slices.
Profit is shown in dollars on $100 bets. The pages we read did not say whether that figure is net of the price of the picks, which a buyer pays on top.
record: Watchdog graded sample, new 22 Nov 2026. SportsCapping does not publish a complete, time stamped log we can audit, so we built a sample from public posts that carry their plays. Watchdog captures X accounts and forum threads that post or repost picks; the ones naming SportsCapping most often were betfirmsjack, EDMrager, mma-expert, TheGodOfCappers. From 20 Nov 2026 to 20 Nov 2026 we took every play our parser could read inside a SportsCapping block, kept only those posted before the game started, removed repeats, and graded each one against the final score at one unit risked, at the odds shown or -110 when none were shown.
Result: 2 plays, 2 won, 0 lost, +1.83 units, a return of +91.3% per unit risked. By month: November 2 won, 0 lost, +1.83 units.
What it means: 2 decided plays is far too few to judge.
What a buyer can verify independently: nothing we could find. We found no full, time stamped pick log kept by an outside party and no monitoring service result for the marketplace as a whole.

What SportsCapping publishes: the FAQ says every pick is graded automatically against final scores and that a full history is on each handicapper profile. Its 2026 season board on 20 Nov 2026 listed 31 handicappers, every one of them in profit, with 34,488 picks between them. A board that shows only winners does not tell you how many of the 76 handicappers on the roster are behind.

The same grading appears on other storefronts. BetFirm's leaderboard uses the SportsCapping "Sc Score" column and its buy buttons go to the SportsCapping cart with an affiliate code. CappersPicks sends account sign ups to SportsCapping with a referral code. PicksDepot, the sister site of OffshoreInsiders, shows a leaderboard whose top five rows matched SportsCapping's exactly on 20 Nov 2026. None of these is a second, independent check.

We found no court or regulator action involving SportsCapping or Boyd Information Group in our searches. BBB lists Boyd Information Group as not accredited and not rated, with one complaint in three years.

our_data.text: In this edition no SportsCapping handicapper is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how these handicappers perform.
our_data.context: For scale: SportsCapping listings feature runs such as 27-10 or 23-9 over 30 days.

customers_intro: Independent buyer evidence on SportsCapping is thin. The main pool is 10 App Store reviews of the SportsCapping app from 2015 to 2025 and one BBB complaint from 2026. CapperTek has no reviews and the Google Play app shows no written reviews we could read. The Reddit archive's full text search failed on 17 and 20 Nov 2026, so the Reddit check relies on our saved library of earlier downloads, which found only promotion. Unhappy buyers are the likeliest to write, so this shows what goes wrong for some buyers, not how many.

customers.text: We found 11 buyer posts in two places over 11 years. Of 10 App Store reviews from 2015 to 2025, seven are negative (one of them a sarcastic five star review that says to bet against every pick): users say the paid picks lost, that the posted stats did not match their own results, that a free replacement for a losing guaranteed package also lost, and that support was by email only with no phone. Two are positive (a long time customer praising a support staffer, and a short 2017 rave) and one, from 2016, is a neutral first impression. The 2026 BBB complaint said a paid $399.95 season pass was never switched on; the company blamed a system fault, activated it backdated and offered a refund, and the buyer accepted. Searches of Sportsbook Review, TheRX, Covers and Reddit found no buyer thread about the marketplace. No buyer posted a tracked record either way.
A one star App Store reviewer warned against buying. They said a losing package is replaced with another package that can also lose, so the buyer is out both the pick price and the bets.
A one star reviewer said support by email did not solve their problems, complained that there is no phone number, and recommended a different handicapper instead.
A five star reviewer said they have used SportsCapping for many years and found a member of the support team very helpful.
A five star review that is sarcastic in substance: "Just fade every pick." The reviewer said betting against the picks had paid well.

Three reviews say the same thing in different words: one user tracked the picks at 1 and 10 after following them, one tested the experts and lost a lot, and one said the experts are poor and their stats do not add up.
A five star reviewer called the app's selections the best in the world. The review gives no detail or record.

A BBB complaint said a $399.95 season pass bought on 5 Sep 2026 was charged but not delivered, and that several emails went unanswered. The business replied that a system fault left the pass inactive, that it switched the pass on dated back to the purchase, and that it offered a partial or full refund. BBB lists the complaint as resolved.
The only Reddit post our archive search found that names SportsCapping is a handicapper's own free play post linking to his SportsCapping profile. It is promotion, not a buyer review.

CapperTek lists SportsCapping.com with no reviews or complaints. Web searches on 20 Nov 2026 found no Sportsbook Review, Covers or TheRX thread reviewing the marketplace, and our saved Reddit library found no buyer discussion. We did not read Trustpilot.

conflicts: SportsCapping grades and publishes the records of the handicappers it sells and earns money on every sale. The About page invites handicappers to "start earning commission on every pick you sell." The scorekeeper and the store are the same company.

The same platform supplies other storefronts. BetFirm and CappersPicks send buyers to SportsCapping with affiliate or referral codes in the links, and PicksDepot shows the same leaderboard. Rankings that appear on one of these sites are not an outside check on another.

Several handicappers sold here also run or sell through their own sites, such as Joe Duffy at OffshoreInsiders and Big Al McMordie at BigAl.com, so the same picks can carry different prices and records in different places.
strengths: Every price is posted, the cheapest picks start at $25, and the FAQ says nothing auto renews.
Guarantees are applied automatically, with no claim to file.
Listings show winning week or season counts next to the hot window, which lets a careful buyer see the weaker long run.
The season leaderboard shows full year records with return on investment, not just win rate.
A BBB complaint in 2026 was answered within a day and resolved with a refund offer.
concerns: All records are graded by the company that sells the picks, though the app listing calls them "independently tracked." No outside monitor found.
The guarantee is a replacement package or extra time, never cash, and refunds are case by case.
Pick titles and banners lead with 30 day windows and hot runs; full season returns on the site's own board are mostly 1% to 3%.
The season board shows only handicappers in profit, so losing handicappers are not visible there.
Most of the buyer reviews we found were negative, though the sample is small.
Support is by email, ticket or chat; reviewers and the BBB complainant said they could not reach anyone quickly.
checklist: Open the handicapper's full history, not the listing window, and count every pick for the last 12 months.
Read the winning weeks count next to every hot run. Fewer than half winning weeks is a warning.
Count units and dollars, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Remember the guarantee is more picks from the same handicapper, not your money back.
Check your account after any Monthly Club purchase to confirm it will not renew.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get, and give a handicapper a few hundred picks before you judge.
faq: It is a real marketplace that delivers the picks it sells, posts every price and names Boyd Information Group as the company behind it. We could not verify that its handicappers win over time, because every record is graded by SportsCapping itself.
What does the Watchdog sample of SportsCapping show?
We graded 2 of their plays that were posted publicly before the game started, 20 Nov 2026 to 20 Nov 2026: 2 won, 0 lost, +1.83 units at one unit each. That is too few plays to judge.

On 20 Nov 2026 single picks and small packs cost $25 to $50, a weekend of football picks from one handicapper cost $99, and the Monthly Club cost $199. Long passes for top names ran up to $1,999.95 for a year.
Not in cash. A losing guaranteed package earns a free replacement package or extra time, applied automatically. The FAQ says refunds are reviewed case by case, and credits cannot be cashed out.
No. The app listing says the records are independently tracked, but the FAQ says SportsCapping grades every pick itself, and sister storefronts such as BetFirm and PicksDepot show the same numbers.
Who is the best handicapper on SportsCapping?
By the site's own 2026 board on 20 Nov 2026, Brooke Bennett led on profit at 1220-1092-56, a 3.2% return. That is a small edge; most of the hot runs on the homepage are 30 day windows.

Only if a handicapper's full history, not a hot window, shows a profit over hundreds of picks after the price of the picks. At -110 odds you need about 52.4% just to break even, and the site's own season board shows even its leaders only a few percent ahead.
